The hotel itself is great—friendly staff, a convenient location, and overall a pleasant stay. Unfortunately, the "complimentary one-hour bike rental" included in the resort fee felt misleading and poorly communicated.

When we checked in, we specifically asked the front desk about the bike rental benefit. We were told that the complimentary bikes were located just outside the lobby, and no additional instructions or requirements were mentioned.

The next morning, when we tried to use the bikes, we were required to enter a credit card. Since that wasn't mentioned before, we went back to the front desk and waited in line to ask about it. The staff member told us this was normal, explaining that the first hour was complimentary and charges would only apply if we exceeded that time limit.

Based on that information, we entered our credit card details. We were then charged $16 per person. We assumed this was a temporary hold or deposit that would be refunded after returning the bikes within the complimentary period.

At checkout, however, a different front desk employee informed us that we were supposed to enter a promotional code printed on a small card, in extremely tiny font. Because we hadn't used that code, we were charged the full rental fee. Even worse, the hotel was unable or unwilling to refund the charges, despite the fact that we had specifically asked for instructions beforehand and were never told about the promo code.

Charging guests for a benefit that is advertised as complimentary because of a hidden promo code requirement is disappointing. If a benefit included in the resort fee requires a special code, that information should be clearly explained at check-in—not buried in tiny print and discovered only after guests have already been charged.

Great hotel, but this experience left a bad impression and felt unnecessarily deceptive.

A Disappointing Anniversary: Inconsistent Service & Poor Management

We stayed for 2 nights for our anniversary, and while there were highlights, this property is showing its age and lacks the basic standards of the Ritz-Carlton brand.

The Room & Housekeeping (The "Ugly"):
The hotel is dated and, frankly, one of the least attractive Ritz properties we’ve seen. We were upgraded to a 1-bedroom suite, but it was filthy. There was dust and someone else’s makeup under the TV stand that stayed there our entire stay. We complained on the first night, but the Housekeeping Manager didn't return our call until 5 minutes before we checked out on Day 3. What can you even do at that point?

Service Failures:
* Check-in: A staff member pulled a newly arrived guest to the front of a long line because they "just got off a flight" (as did the rest of us). A pathetic offer of water didn't fix the frustration.
* Anniversary: Promised champagne/strawberries took 3 follow-ups and 2 days to arrive.
* Pool: Service is slow; we were completely ignored while staff handed out fruit to everyone else.
* Spa: Short-staffed and unable to accommodate us. I appreciate that they called multiple times a day to give us staffing updates, but a hotel of this caliber should be prepared.

Dining & The "Good":
* Club Lounge: The standout of the trip. Amazing service and great F&B selection. This is the only place that felt like a Ritz.
* The Beach: Slow service, but the fish tacos and guacamole were incredible.
* Zaytinya: Overpriced and mediocre. Good cocktails, but disappointing for a Jose Andres spot.
* Room Service: The breakfast attendant was amazing and the food was great (though $14 for 2 eggs with no toast is a bit much).

The Verdict:
The 20% automatic service charge seems to have removed any incentive for the staff to provide actual "luxury" service. Aside from the Club Lounge and the beach food, this was a major letdown.

Just checked in for the next 2 nights and wanted to leave a practical note for other travellers—mainly so expectations match the product.

Positives so far: Front desk staff has been polite, calm, and responsive. When we raised the issue below, they gave a clear explanation without being dismissive.

Key concern (functionality, not aesthetics): The guestroom lighting is very limited. There is no ceiling light and the room relies largely on a small number of lamps. Even with every light switched on, the overall brightness is still low. That matters because lighting isn’t just “ambience”—it affects basic room usability (reading, working on a laptop, packing, finding items, and getting ready at night).

We asked frontdesk staff Mark whether a brighter room was available, and were told this is the design/theme across the hotel and there were no alternative options. He diligently sent an engineer to ensure the existing 2 lamps are working.

Who this will suit: If you prefer a dim, moodier aesthetic and don’t plan to do much in-room, you may be fine.

Who should think twice: If you value practical, well-lit rooms (families, people working while travelling, anyone needing clear lighting), factor this in before booking.

Overall: Reasonable staff and straightforward communication, but the lighting setup significantly reduces day-to-day comfort and room functionality for us.

text.text: The Sagamore is an interesting conundrum - on the positive side, the beach access is great. The free chairs and towels are also nice (although I think this is fairly standard for a beach-adjacent hotel). The service was also prompt as in people responded or showed up quickly when requested. However, for a hotel that is supposedly “4 stars”, here’s what I think was lacking: first - the rooms are a bit odd, definitely not “4 stars”. They are dated and sparse - very little in the way of amenities or even furniture. The “beach view” I had was actually just a view to adjacent concrete building with spray painted writing all over it (which was made more comical when I got an email after my stay asking me to rate my “beach view room”). Second - the cleaning was a bit lackluster. The room did not seem overly “clean” from the get go and when we had it cleaned, the tile floors always had hair remaining on them or sand. The bathroom never felt particularly clean and the table and chairs had stains and marks all over them. They also left a dirty cleaning rag on top of my wife’s cosmetics case and hairbrush the last day we were there. Further, each day the staff seemed to want to get out of cleaning our room and seemed like they were trying to get me to confirm I didn’t need cleaning each day in the morning when they came by. Third, the walls were like paper - there was constant noise from late evening to early morning and honestly it could by hard to sleep through it. Not to mention, there seemed to be ongoing construction at the hotel or building next door and we had no forewarning. One day my wife went to open the blinds in the morning and there were several construction workers standing right outside our 2nd floor window.  Fourth, the room has a wet bar / kitchen set up but it is completely devoid of any dishes or silverware. It was noted that you can request it, which I did, and was told I could have plastic utensils and plastic plates. That is all fine, but again, not a 4-star hotel experience. For context, I have stayed in probably 100+ hotels all over the world ranging from 3-5 star so I think I have a good sample of what 4-star in the USA generally looks/feels like. Overall, the experience felt like a lower end 3 star hotel trying to stretch to obtain a 4 star rating while  spending the least amount of money on renovations and amenities to actually deliver a 4 star experience.

Unfortunately, staying here wasn't the greatest experience. First and foremost, there was never any hot water. It did get mildly warm for ~2/20 showers during my 10 day stay. Enduring icy showers every day, however, was not the best.

The air conditioning barely worked, leaving me sweating in my room all night. I had to go out and buy USB fans just to sleep comfortably. Adjusting the thermostat didn’t seem to make a difference at all, I wondered if it was even connected to anything.

The TV setup was a letdown as well. There’s no HDMI port or smart TV features, so I couldn’t connect any of my devices or watch anything at all during my entire stay. When I searched behind the TV for an HDMI port, I was met with a really thick layer of sticky dust—it was quite unappealing to dig through to look for a port. I figured it was standard for most hotels to have at least one hdmi port available, without it the TV is just useless wall decor.

On the subject of cleanliness, the overall condition of my room was pretty poor. There were actual visible dust clumps everywhere: on the walls, lamps, and even in the fridge, others were hanging off fixtures and from the ceiling. It was really pretty gross and looked like the room hadn't been cleaned thoroughly in months or years. Most of the appliances were broken or had other issues, and the towel bar and bathroom mirror were starting to fall off the wall.

You could hear everything from the upstairs guests, somehow even their phones vibrating on a table. While this noise alone from neighbors wouldn't have been that big of an issue, the noise from the cleaning staff slamming doors nonstop throughout the day, seemingly as hard as they could, and starting daily around **6 AM**, made it difficult to get quality sleep or enjoy any kind of sleep in on your vacation. I noticed others complaining about outside external noise in reviews, but I found that to be expected in South Beach and wasn’t particularly bothered by it.

On the brighter side, the rooms were a decent size and furnished well. The bed was comfortable, and the limited staff interactions I had were very friendly and helpful every time. The location is good, and the pool area was really very nice.

A heads-up: the front door locks at night, and staff isn’t always at the front desk. My key cards stopped working one day, so if I hadn't forgotten something and had to go back to my room in the morning, I could have easily been locked out that night.

In short, while there were some positive aspects to my stay, and while it certainly wasn't *terrible*, these issues really overshadowed my experience, particularly the lack of A/C, hot water, and the all-day door slamming. I’ve stayed at several other hotels on Collins with much better experiences.

Stayed for the weekend. The decor was lovely, with vintage photographs on the walls and dark flooring that added old-world charm. The bathroom was beautiful, and the bed was comfortable. The staff were very kind and genuinely tried to help and resolve any issues. Breakfast was a nice touch — good coffee, eggs with potatoes, and a super friendly server. There’s even a partial ocean view from the rooftop deck, and the location is great — an easy walk to everything.

We were disappointed to find that the main restaurant facing Collins Street was under construction — we had been looking forward to relaxing there after our days out. The lounge on the other side was closed as well, and even the front coffee bar wasn’t open. We were not informed about the remodeling when we booked well in advance.

Our room had a spacious patio, but the daybed needed cleaning. My side of the bed had no nightstand, and overall, the room could have used a deep clean. Unfortunately, the value didn’t match the experience.

Thank you anyway, and best of luck to the team.

One might expect to have a peaceful and relaxing stay in a hotel, particularly in South Beach; however, my experience at the James Hotel in Miami, FL, was quite the opposite.

I arrived at approximately 3:30 PM on December 13, 2025, hoping to receive my room thirty minutes prior to the 4:00 PM check-in time (Confirmation # 9078866105381, initials J.A.).

The receptionist, who introduced herself as the "daughter of the hotel's owner," informed me she would impose a $10 fee for storing my bag, even for a few minutes, a $10 fee for "early" parking, and a $50 fee for early check-in. Interestingly, the lobby was empty, there was only one car in the parking lot, and it was only a few minutes before the check-in time of 4:00 PM. Furthermore, she mentioned a $50 per hour charge for late check-out. Her condescending and harsh demeanor was clearly intended to intimidate me, ultimately ruining my weekend.

While I understand hotels have their policies, this kind of rude behavior towards a paying guest is unacceptable and not a proper way to conduct business.

This individual's inappropriate behavior and condescending attitude are intolerable. Guests should not be treated in such a manner. It is particularly concerning as she claimed to be the "daughter of the owner" and threatened to cancel my reservation when I inquired about her name, which she refused to provide.

Although the room rate was relatively modest and the additional charges minimal, I see no reason to patronize this hotel.t is a fact that the hospitality industry is struggling and having a difficult time coping. I don't like writing negative reviews --- but, this is something that everybody should  know about.

Thank goodness AMEX Travel was able to cancel my booking and helped me through this ordeal.

Lastly, this James Hotel doesn't even look like it has clean & nice rooms since everything seems deary from the outside and at the lobby.

I decided to take the next flight back to NYC since I cannot possibly stay in South Beach with this unsettling experience in my mind.

Air conditioning doesn't work and manager by far the rudest woman I've met.

Air conditioning didn't work in our initial room and asked for this to be looked at the next day. Reception staff were kind and helpful and said they would see to it. We got back later that evening and the room was exactly the same temperature. So went back to reception and again receptionist was helpful and provided us with an extra room (next to the original room).

Obviously the new room was extremely hot as it hadn't had the air conditioning running whatsoever so given the late hour I decided to move my belongings across to the new room and try to sleep as the room cooled. The new room didn't cool and I woke up drenched in sweat. My original room was still cooler than the new one so I went to try and sleep in there instead as it was now 4.00 in the morning.

The manager then woke me and my partner up SHOUTING that we leave the room. I explained the situation and the manager did not apologize for her tone or the condition of the room. She was totally out of order and even when she had calmed herself down did not apologize for her tone when talking to me or my partner.

We truly tired to be understanding about the condition of the room and I would not have left a negative review had the manager now been totally out of order. We cancelled our future booking for that hotel and I would urge you to do the same.
